The image displays an axial cross-section of the thorax with high spatial resolution, clearly distinguishing cortical bone (bright white), soft tissue (gray), and air-filled lung parenchyma (black). This tomographic appearance with Hounsfield-unit-based contrast is characteristic of Computed Tomography (CT), not a projectional X-ray or MRI.
